article_title: Revisiting the trajectory of medical students' empathy, and impact of gender, specialty preferences and nationality: a systematic review.
citation: Andersen Freja Allerelli, Johansen Ann-Sofie Bering, Søndergaard Jens, Andersen Christina Maar, Assing Hvidt Elisabeth. (2020). Revisiting the trajectory of medical students' empathy, and impact of gender, specialty preferences and nationality: a systematic review. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-020-1964-5
title: Jefferson Scale of Empathy – Student Version (JSPE-S)
description: The JSPE-S is the self-report instrument used by most included studies; the review describes it as measuring affective empathy and studying "the empathic relationship between the medical student and the patient". It consists of 20 items on a 7-point Likert scale, with a minimum of 20 and a maximum of 140 points, where a high score indicates a more empathic orientation. All cross-sectional studies except four, and all longitudinal studies except one, employed the JSPE-S. The review notes the scale focuses on thoughts and not actions, citing Sulzer.
requirements: Validated scales; the review notes all studies except one employed validated scales, and flags one study applying the English validated JSPE-S to students without English as their native language
constraints: Self-reporting questionnaires introduce reporting bias; self-reported empathy has only a vague association with the patient-physician relationship in the clinical setting, per the review's cited literature
target_learning_goals: measuring empathy levels across educational years, gender, specialty preference and nationality
examples: Cross-sectional sample sizes of included studies using the JSPE-S ranged from 129 to 5521 participants, and longitudinal samples from 72 to 1653
key_sources: Andersen Freja Allerelli, Johansen Ann-Sofie Bering, Søndergaard Jens, Andersen Christina Maar, Assing Hvidt Elisabeth. (2020). Revisiting the trajectory of medical students' empathy, and impact of gender, specialty preferences and nationality: a systematic review. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-020-1964-5

article_title: Selecting for empathy? A cross-sectional study on empathy and empathic care intentions in newly enrolled dentistry, medicine, nursing, and pharmacy students in Singapore to inform admissions and training.
citation: Müller AM, Tan CGL, Lau STL, Gallagher PJ. (2026). Selecting for empathy? A cross-sectional study on empathy and empathic care intentions in newly enrolled dentistry, medicine, nursing, and pharmacy students in Singapore to inform admissions and training. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-09510-2
title: Jefferson Scale of Empathy, Healthcare Professions Student version (JSE-HPS)
description: The JSE-HPS is a 20-item instrument rated on a 7-point Likert scale focusing on cognitive dimensions of empathy, described by the article as "a widely used and psychometrically robust instrument in healthcare education research". Total scores range from 20 to 140, with higher scores indicating greater empathy. The study used it to measure empathy among 646 newly enrolled healthcare students, yielding a median score of 109 (IQR: 102–116).
requirements: A licence for the instrument; the article notes funding was received for the licence of the JSE-HPS.
constraints: The article notes interpreting scores is challenging due to the absence of population-specific normative data across disciplines; published normative data have focused exclusively on Medicine students.
target_learning_goals: Assessment of cognitive empathy attitudes and beliefs related to patient-centred care
examples: The study administered the JSE-HPS to 646 newly enrolled Dentistry, Medicine, Nursing, and Pharmacy students via an online survey before and during the first weeks of the academic year.
key_sources: Müller AM, Tan CGL, Lau STL, Gallagher PJ. (2026). Selecting for empathy? A cross-sectional study on empathy and empathic care intentions in newly enrolled dentistry, medicine, nursing, and pharmacy students in Singapore to inform admissions and training. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-09510-2
